question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(8,{5}^{2}),$ compute $P(X<6).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2743\,$ | $\,0.2709\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3085\,$ | $\,0.3050\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3446\,$ | $\,0.3409\,$ | $\,0.3372\,$ |

$P(X<6)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =8$ and $\sigma =5.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<6) & =P(Z<\frac{6-8}{5}) \\  & =P\,(Z<-\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.4) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.4) \\  & =Φ(-0.4)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/904c15923a1411ec46e91474905da38fff7d0b80f07a922efaf89023e0ed42db.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(-0.4)=0.3446.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<6)=0.3446.
$$
